metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concurrency/idempotency expectation for reset_attempts + forced enqueue (e.g. the _rebar_force + dedup short-circuit tolerates duplicate enqueues, and reset is idempotent) so concurrent/duplicate recheck-review triggers are safe.
evidence: 'dedup.reset_attempts(change_id, current_revision)' followed by enqueue with _rebar_force — two operations, not stated to be atomic
No handling for two recheck-review comments arriving close together, or a recheck-review racing an in-flight automatic escalation
review_attempts ledger is consumed by 0347 (per 'Relationship to 0347') — a cross-path shared record
findings.finding: The attempts-budget reset (dedup.reset_attempts DELETE) is shared state mutated by both this contributor path and 0347's automatic-retry path, but the plan does not address concurrency/idempotency of reset+enqueue under concurrent or duplicate triggers.
scenarios: Contributor double-comments recheck-review — two resets + two forced enqueues of the same revision
recheck-review reset races 0347's escalation increment, re-arming or clobbering budget in an unexpected order
findings.suggested_fix: Note that reset_attempts is an idempotent DELETE and the _rebar_force enqueue is deduped by the existing force-path guard, so N near-simultaneous recheck-review comments collapse to at most one in-flight forced review.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify (and test) the behavior when `get_change_messages` fails/times out or returns a malformed/empty message list — fail-closed to a refusal-or-retry reply with a greppable marker, never a silent drop or unhandled worker exception.
evidence: 'fetch the bot's change messages via GET /a/changes/{id}/messages'
The plan enumerates refusal/acceptance/no-op/unparseable outcomes but never the get_change_messages FAILURE outcome — an absence in an otherwise thorough non-happy-path enumeration.
AC1/AC2/AC3 test enqueue, refusal, and no-op but no AC covers a transient Gerrit-fetch failure.
findings.finding: The eligibility path fetches change messages via `GET /a/changes/{id}/messages` but the plan does not specify behavior when that REST call fails/times out (network error, 404, malformed response). Because eligibility is decided from this fetch, a failed fetch has no defined outcome — the contributor may receive no reply and the trigger may silently drop, or an exception may bubble up unhandled in the worker.
findings.location: Approach step 3, 'Eligibility — decided privileged-side from durable Gerrit state' / step 5 gerrit_client helpers
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step: on a message-fetch error, log a distinct marker (e.g. RETRIGGER_FETCH_ERROR) and post a short 'could not determine review state, try again shortly' reply; add a parametrized test for the fetch-error branch.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how duplicate/concurrent `recheck-review` triggers on the same change/revision are handled (e.g. collapse to a single forced re-review, or explicitly accept the redundant run as harmless-because-serialized) so the force-path's dedup bypass does not silently fan out.
evidence: Plan: 'enqueue the change's current revision with the existing `_rebar_force` marker (the `/rerun` force path — bypasses dedup + existing-vote short-circuits...)'
voter.py:42-45 — the single-flight lock relies on 'the dedup/Gerrit check inside the lock then makes the later ones a no-op skip', which the force path deliberately skips
This is wasteful (redundant forced review) but fail-closed and serialized, so low severity — G6 nonetheless flags concurrent/duplicate handling as an edge case to state
findings.finding: The plan does not address concurrent or duplicate `recheck-review` comments on the same change/revision. Because acceptance enqueues with the `_rebar_force` marker — which by design bypasses the dedup + existing-vote short-circuits — two near-simultaneous (or a repeated) trigger each call `reset_attempts` and enqueue a redundant forced re-review; the per-(change,rev) single-flight lock serializes them but the force path skips the no-op skip that would otherwise collapse the second, so duplicate full reviews run.
scenarios: Two contributors comment `recheck-review` within the same second
A contributor double-posts or edits the comment, producing two comment-added events
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to step 3 'On acceptance' noting the intended behavior — either that a redundant trigger is acceptable because the per-(change,rev) lock serializes and a second forced review is idempotent/harmless, or that the trigger de-dups on an already-queued force event for that revision.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the GET /a/changes/{id}/messages ChangeMessageInfo response shape against a live capture — specifically the `_revision_number` field and the `author` account-identity form used to match the bot — in a committed fixture, alongside the already-planned `Patch Set N:` preamble fixture, since the entire eligibility gate keys on those two fields.
evidence: Plan quote: 'select the latest entry whose `_revision_number` equals the current patchset AND whose author is the bot account'

Plan pins only the preamble: 'verify the exact preamble shape against a live capture during implementation and pin it in a fixture' — no equivalent verification is stated for the `_revision_number` / `author` selector fields

GerritClient today does not call GET .../messages (gerrit_client.py docstring lists only patch/review/events-log endpoints), so the response shape is a genuinely NEW surface — Partially-verified: the endpoint exists but its field names/author-resolution are unconfirmed against a live capture

The bot-author match is the loop-guard's twin: if the `author` object shape (e.g. `_account_id` vs `username` vs `email`) is mis-assumed, the selector silently picks the wrong message and eligibility is decided from the wrong tag
findings.finding: The eligibility decision depends on the GET /a/changes/{id}/messages (ChangeMessageInfo) response carrying a per-message `_revision_number` field AND an `author` object resolvable to the bot account, but the plan routes ONLY the `Patch Set N:` preamble text to live-capture verification — the two selector fields the whole eligibility gate keys on are asserted as settled without a verification step or fixture.
findings.location: Approach step 3, 'Eligibility' bullet ('select the latest entry whose _revision_number equals the current patchset AND whose author is the bot account'); AC2b
scenarios: Gerrit returns the bot author keyed by `_account_id` (an int) rather than a username/email the code compares against, so no message ever matches and every recheck-review fails open to a fresh review even on a real finding
A message's `_revision_number` is absent on some ChangeMessageInfo forms (e.g. older change-message entries), so the 'latest entry for current patchset' selection silently falls through
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the live-capture step already scoped for the preamble to also capture and fixture a real ChangeMessageInfo entry, and specify which author field the bot-account match uses (e.g. `author._account_id` compared to the configured bot account id, not a username string); add a fixture-backed unit test asserting the correct message is selected for the current revision.

findings.finding: The eligibility parser is specified to rest on 'the `_TAG_SUFFIXES` vocabulary, test-asserted' AND to treat `merge-review` as a parseable coverage-gap sub-reason, but `_TAG_SUFFIXES` does not contain a `merge-review` key — that tag is emitted as a hardcoded literal outside the vocabulary.
findings.location: Approach → Step 3, 'Eligibility' bullet ('parse its first-line tag (the `_TAG_SUFFIXES` vocabulary, test-asserted) ... every coverage-gap sub-reason (including `merge-review` ...)')
findings.suggested_fix: State that the parser must match the coverage-gap sub-reason token INSIDE `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (<reason>)]` (a superset of `_TAG_SUFFIXES` that also includes the voter.py `merge-review` literal and tolerates the `(merge-change, N integrated commit(s))` suffix), and add `merge-review` to a single shared reason set (or centralize the merge tag through `_TAG_SUFFIXES`) so the 'test-asserted vocabulary' claim holds.

findings.finding: The eligibility parser is specified to parse the current-revision tag against 'the _TAG_SUFFIXES vocabulary (test-asserted)', but `merge-review` — which the plan repeatedly names as an eligible coverage-gap sub-reason — is not a key in `_TAG_SUFFIXES`; its tag is emitted by a hardcoded string in `voter.py::_merge_coverage_gap_decision`, and the `(merge-change, N integrated commit(s))` suffix variant is appended outside `_TAG_SUFFIXES`. A parser keyed strictly to the `_TAG_SUFFIXES` vocabulary would not recognize either, so a `recheck-review` on a merge-review-blocked change would fall through the tag match the plan relies on.
findings.location: Approach step 3, 'Eligibility' bullet ('parse its first-line tag (the _TAG_SUFFIXES vocabulary, test-asserted)'); AC1
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the parser as: extract the `coverage-gap (<reason>)` token from the bot's first-line tag (tolerating the trailing `(merge-change, N …)` suffix), and treat the ONLY ineligible reason as `finding`; note that `merge-review` is emitted by `_merge_coverage_gap_decision` outside `_TAG_SUFFIXES` and is therefore included explicitly.

findings.finding: The eligibility parser is specified against the `_TAG_SUFFIXES` vocabulary, but the plan lists `merge-review` as an eligible coverage-gap sub-reason — and `merge-review` is NOT a member of `_TAG_SUFFIXES`; it is a separately hardcoded tag string produced by `_merge_coverage_gap_decision` in voter.py. A parser keyed strictly to `_TAG_SUFFIXES` cannot classify a `merge-review` first-line tag, leaving that eligibility case under-specified or misrouted.
findings.suggested_fix: Define eligibility as: refuse only a first-line tag matching `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding...]`; treat ANY other `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (...)]` tag (including `merge-review`, which is not in `_TAG_SUFFIXES`) and PASS as eligible.

findings.finding: The plan states eligibility parses 'the `_TAG_SUFFIXES` vocabulary (test-asserted)' and lists `merge-review` as an eligible state, but `merge-review` is NOT a member of `_TAG_SUFFIXES` — it is a hardcoded tag literal in voter.py, so a parser bound strictly to that enum has an undefined outcome for the merge-review tag the plan requires to be eligible.
findings.location: Approach §3 'Eligibility' bullet ("parse its first-line tag (the `_TAG_SUFFIXES` vocabulary, test-asserted)" and "including `merge-review`")
findings.suggested_fix: State the match rule as: refuse iff the first-line suffix begins with `BLOCK — finding`; treat every other `[LLM-Review: ...]` first-line tag (including the voter.py `merge-review` literal not in `_TAG_SUFFIXES`) as eligible — decoupling eligibility from strict `_TAG_SUFFIXES` membership.

findings.finding: The finding-refusal check is scoped to the exact tag `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]`, but a real finding on a MERGE change renders with a suffix INSIDE the tag: `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, N integrated commit(s))]`. If the refusal match is exact/prefix-naive, a merge-change finding would not match and would be wrongly ACCEPTED for re-review — defeating the asserted security property on merge changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify by the tag's sub-reason token (`finding` vs `coverage-gap (...)`) rather than exact-string equality, so `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, ...)]` is still recognized as a finding and refused; assert this in AC2.

findings.finding: The plan's post-comment-without-vote helper defers between two non-equivalent Gerrit REST forms ('post_vote with value 0 or the bare /review message form, whichever the API offers cleanly'), and one of them (value=0) writes the LLM-Review label — contradicting the plan's own stated security invariant that this path 'never touches the vote' / posts 'a message, never a vote'. The vote-free capability is asserted but not verified.
findings.location: Approach §5 (Gerrit client) and Security property; Scope: gerrit_client.py
findings.suggested_fix: Add a dedicated post_message(change_id, revision, message) helper that POSTs {tag, notify:NONE, message} with NO 'labels' field (verified no-vote), and state in §5 that value=0 is disallowed on this path.

findings.finding: Eligibility hinges on fetching 'the bot's latest change message for the CURRENT revision and parsing its first-line tag', but the specific Gerrit REST surface (endpoint, per-revision filtering, and whether ChangeMessageInfo.message preserves the [LLM-Review: ...] first line rather than prepending a 'Patch Set N:' header) is unverified. A mismatch silently breaks the tag parse that decides accept-vs-refuse.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture a live ChangeMessageInfo fixture from the running Gerrit (as done for the merge path in tests/fixtures/review_bot_merge/) and pin the tag-extraction against it.

findings.finding: The plan's finding-refusal rule ('refuse only a current-revision `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]` tag') does not specify exact-vs-prefix tag matching, but on a MERGE change the finding tag renders with an in-tag suffix — `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, N integrated commit(s))]` — so an exact-equality match against the bare `BLOCK — finding` suffix would miss it and wrongly treat a real merge finding as eligible.
findings.suggested_fix: State: refusal triggers when the first-line suffix STARTS WITH `BLOCK — finding` (covering both the bare and `(merge-change, ...)` variants); add a dedicated test for `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, 3 integrated commit(s))]` under AC2.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify failure handling for get_change_messages/post_comment (timeout, error, empty/malformed message list): fail-closed vs fail-open decision and a log marker for each.
evidence: Plan specifies fail-open only for 'an UNPARSEABLE or absent tag' — a parse-side condition
No stated behavior when 'GET /a/changes/{id}/messages' errors, times out, or returns an empty/malformed list
post_comment failure (reply not posted) has no fallback or log marker specified
findings.finding: The new Gerrit REST calls the eligibility path depends on (get_change_messages, post_comment) have no specified failure handling — a fetch error or unexpected message-list shape has undefined behavior, unlike the parse side which is explicitly fail-open.
scenarios: Gerrit is slow/unreachable when a contributor comments recheck-review — the worker's behavior (crash, silent drop, retry) is undefined
messages fetch succeeds but the bot has posted no message on the current revision (empty selection)
findings.suggested_fix: State that a messages-fetch error logs a marker and defers (no enqueue, no budget reset — the contributor can retry), and that an empty bot-message selection is treated as the vote-less/absent-tag ELIGIBLE case already described.
